lines.text: America imported a record $420.8 billion in August.
lines.say: America imported a record four hundred twenty-one billion dollars in August.

lines.text: That's an all-time high, per the government's trade report out October 6.
lines.say: That's an all-time high, and it blew open the trade gap.

lines.text: The trade deficit jumped from $92.8 billion in July to $105.6 billion in August, the widest since early 2025.
lines.say: The trade deficit jumped from about ninety-three billion dollars in July to about one hundred six billion, the widest since early twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Among the import jumps: crude oil +$3.3B, gold +$3.1B, computer chips +$2.4B.
lines.say: What jumped? Crude oil imports rose about three point three billion dollars, gold three point one, and computer chips two point four.

lines.text: The gap is imports minus exports. Exports rose too, to $315.2 billion, but more slowly.
lines.say: The gap is imports minus exports, and exports rose too, to about three hundred fifteen billion, but more slowly.

lines.text: The twist: January to August, the deficit is 19.9% smaller than the same months of 2025, when imports surged ahead of tariffs.
lines.say: The twist? January through August, the gap is about twenty percent smaller than in twenty twenty-five, when companies rushed imports in before tariffs.

lines.text: A trade deficit isn't a debt. It's buying versus selling, and imports are subtracted when GDP is calculated.
lines.say: A trade deficit isn't a bill anyone pays back. It's buying versus selling, though imports get subtracted when GDP is counted.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: America imported a record $420.8 billion in August
post.ig:
America imported a record $420.8 billion in August 2026.
The trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion from $92.8 billion in July, the widest since early 2025.
Imports of crude oil (+$3.3B), gold (+$3.1B) and computer chips (+$2.4B) all jumped.
Twist: January-August, the deficit is still 19.9% smaller than the same months of 2025.
Sources: BEA and Census Bureau, Aug 2026 trade report (Oct 6, 2026); Bloomberg.
